implementationPlan.description:
Land apps/daemon/src/journal/journal-contracts.ts plus its one-line bridge `export * from "./journal-contracts.ts";` (a .ts module without its .js bridge is invisible to consumers while tsc and vitest both stay green). This file carries the validation bulk so the service module stays under the per-file cap.
- `JOURNAL_APPEND_COMMAND_KIND` annotated as `RuntimeCommandKind` from @moe/contracts so a typo fails to compile; do NOT add a wire kind.
- `JOURNAL_APPEND_SCHEMA_VERSION = "moe-journal-append/1"`, `JOURNAL_RECORD_VERSION = "moe-attempt-journal/1"`, `JOURNAL_APPEND_EVENT_TYPE = "AttemptJournalAppended"`.
- `JOURNAL_APPEND_PAYLOAD_KEYS = ["attemptAggregateId", "effectId", "entries"]` — EXACTLY these three. projectId, sessionId, leaseRef, graphRef, journalDigest, truthClass and a replacement `journal` are deliberately absent, which is what makes them structurally refused by the seam's `checkPayload` allow-list under ITS `PAYLOAD_SHAPE` code rather than by anything downstream.
- `DAEMON_JOURNAL_APPEND` layer constant, and a frozen closed code list: JOURNAL_REQUEST_MALFORMED, JOURNAL_ENTRY_MALFORMED, JOURNAL_ENTRY_LIST_EMPTY, JOURNAL_BINDING_MISMATCH, JOURNAL_NODE_UNREADABLE, JOURNAL_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE, JOURNAL_RECORD_ABSENT, JOURNAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE, JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED, JOURNAL_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS, JOURNAL_PROJECT_MISMATCH, JOURNAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH.
- `deriveAttemptJournalAggregateId(activationDigest)`: length-framed sha256, same shape as `deriveAttemptReleaseAggregateId`. Keyed on the ACTIVATION DIGEST because that value is server-derived and coherence-checked by the binding reader, so no caller can name a journal stream into existence.
- THE STRICT ENTRY DECODER, and it is load-bearing: `createDeadEndJournal` performs NO shape validation. Its `clonePredicate` switches on `predicate.kind` and returns `undefined` for an unknown kind, and `canonicalSha256` THROWS on `undefined` (`Unsupported canonical value type`). An unvalidated entry therefore CRASHES the command instead of refusing it, and a crash is not a refusal. Decode each entry over own data properties: exact 11 keys (id, kind, failureCode, primaryScope, recipeDigest, baseDigest, environmentDigest, retryPredicate, text, actorId, occurredAt); `kind` must be a member of `DEAD_END_KINDS` IMPORTED from @moe/context (never retyped locally); `retryPredicate` exact-keyed per its `kind` against @moe/context's `FactPredicate`; the three digest fields lowercase hex64; `occurredAt` an ISO instant ending in Z; `text` a bounded string. Anything else -> JOURNAL_ENTRY_MALFORMED. An empty `entries` array -> JOURNAL_ENTRY_LIST_EMPTY.

journal-entry-codec.ts — the decoder, and it is the fence not defence in depth:
- ownData(value, allowed): rejects null/array/non-Object.prototype prototypes, any own symbol key, any accessor or non-enumerable property, and any own-name-count mismatch; every read goes through getOwnPropertyDescriptor and the whole thing is try/catch-wrapped so a revoked proxy answers null instead of throwing. An own `__proto__` key can never survive: the name count check sees 12 names against 11 allowed and refuses before any assignment.
- exact 11 entry keys; kind from DEAD_END_KINDS IMPORTED from @moe/context (never retyped); occurredAt a fixed-width ISO instant ending Z with a real Date.parse; recipeDigest/baseDigest/environmentDigest lowercase hex64; id/actorId/failureCode/primaryScope bounded non-empty; text bounded, may be empty.
- retryPredicate exact-keyed PER ITS OWN KIND against @moe/context's FactPredicate (FACT_VALUE/FACT_VERSION/FACT_DIGEST), including the per-variant operator set, so an unknown predicate kind is a REFUSAL here instead of `clonePredicate` returning undefined and canonicalSha256 throwing.
- Strings must be NFC-identical (two spellings of the same text would otherwise hash to two different journals); -0 is rejected outright since it compares equal to 0 and canonicalises to 0.
- The value handed to createDeadEndJournal is a FRESH plain object this module builds — cloneEntry's spread therefore cannot carry a key, an accessor or a prototype the decoder did not admit.
- DELIBERATELY NO entry-count or text-length cap here beyond hostile ceilings (4096 entries / 64KiB text, both far above MAX_JOURNAL_ENTRY_COUNT=8 and MAX_JOURNAL_TEXT_CHARACTERS=12288): those two limits belong to createDeadEndJournal, which must answer them under ITS OWN JOURNAL_LIMIT_REACHED / DEAD_END_JOURNAL pair. A cap here would answer first and hide that layer entirely.
- Empty entries array -> JOURNAL_ENTRY_LIST_EMPTY, distinct from JOURNAL_ENTRY_MALFORMED. Sparse arrays and arrays with extra own keys are refused by an own-name-count check.

implementationPlan.description:
Land the WRITER in apps/daemon/src/journal/journal-append.ts plus its `export * from "./journal-append.ts";` bridge: `runJournalAppendCommand(store, bytes)`, matching the shape of the other registry-dispatched services (server-assembled request bytes in, `{ok, decision, disposition}` or a refusal out).
Order is the contract, and each stage keeps the refusing layer's OWN code:
1. Decode the request bytes: bounded JSON, exact envelope keys, `kind` and `schemaVersion` match -> JOURNAL_REQUEST_MALFORMED otherwise. projectId, principalId and decidedAt are SERVER facts already stamped by the registry's `requestOf`; never read them from the payload.
2. Payload exact keys per JOURNAL_APPEND_PAYLOAD_KEYS.
3. `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding(store, projectId, payload.effectId, principalId, Date.parse(decidedAt))` from ../activation/activation-ledger-reader.js. Not BOUND -> return ITS code (FOUNDATION_BINDING_LEASE_INACTIVE / _LEASE_EXPIRED / _TERMINAL / _NOT_FOUND / _QUERY_MISMATCH / _PROJECT_MISMATCH ...) and ITS layer VERBATIM. Do not restamp: a stale lease must stay distinguishable from an absent attempt. This one call is what makes the append attempt/session/lease-bound — it requires intent ACTIVE, attempt RUNNING, lease ACTIVE, lease not past its wall deadline, and a coherent activation, all from committed evidence.
4. Derive the durable attempt facts: `store.readEvents(payload.attemptAggregateId)` then `readFoundationActivationHistory(aggregateId, events, projectId)`. Cross-check `record.activationDigest === binding.activationDigest`, `record.effectIntent.intentId === binding.effectId`, `record.lease.ownerSessionRef === binding.sessionId`; any mismatch -> JOURNAL_BINDING_MISMATCH. attemptRef = `record.attempt.attemptId`, leaseRef = `record.lease.leaseId` — the caller's aggregate id only LOCATES; the activation-digest equality is what forbids pointing at someone else's attempt.
5. nodeKey from durable evidence: read `deriveDispatchAggregateId(payload.attemptAggregateId)` (from ../work/foundation-attempt-codec.js), take the exactly-one `FoundationDispatchReserved` event, decode + re-encode + sameBytes, read `nodeKey`. Zero, two, or drifted bytes -> JOURNAL_NODE_UNREADABLE. The RESERVED event is written at dispatch, so it exists for a live attempt.
6. Decode the caller entries with the step-3 strict decoder.
7. Read the CURRENT durable journal (step 5's reader). ABSENT means an empty entry list and is NOT an error here; every other refusal propagates unchanged.
8. `createDeadEndJournal([...current.entries, ...admittedEntries])`. A REFUSED result keeps its own `JOURNAL_LIMIT_REACHED` code and `DEAD_END_JOURNAL` layer verbatim — do not restamp, do not truncate, do not retry with fewer entries.
9. Compose the body from DURABLE facts only: recordVersion, projectId, sessionId, effectId, attemptRef, leaseRef, nodeKey, activationDigest, entries (the ADMITTED, canonically ordered ones), journalDigest (the admitted journal's own digest), truthClass "DAEMON_VERIFIED". Canonical bytes via `encodeFoundationPayload`; drift -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED.
10. Commit ONE event on `deriveAttemptJournalAggregateId(binding.activationDigest)` at `expectedVersion` = current event count, key `{commandId, principalId, projectId}`. Append-only: never rewrite a prior event. Throw or non-EFFECTS_COMMITTED -> JOURNAL_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE.
11. Answer from the reader — never from the value just written.

THE ELEVEN STAGES, each keeping the refusing layer's OWN code:
1. decodeRequest: input must be Uint8Array -> decodeBoundedJsonBytes -> exact 9 envelope keys via the shared `exactKeys` -> kind and schemaVersion must equal JOURNAL_APPEND_COMMAND_KIND / "moe-journal-append/1"; commandId, correlationId, principalId, projectId non-empty; decidedAt parseable. Anything else -> JOURNAL_REQUEST_MALFORMED. projectId/principalId/decidedAt are read from the ENVELOPE the registry's `requestOf` stamped, never from the payload (which structurally cannot carry them).
2. payload exact-keyed against JOURNAL_APPEND_PAYLOAD_KEYS; attemptAggregateId and effectId non-empty.
3. readCurrentEffectSessionBinding(store, projectId, payload.effectId, principalId, Date.parse(decidedAt)). status !== "BOUND" -> `journalRefusal(binding.code, binding.layer)` — ITS code and ITS layer VERBATIM (FOUNDATION_BINDING_LEASE_EXPIRED / _LEASE_INACTIVE / _TERMINAL / _NOT_FOUND / _QUERY_MISMATCH / _PROJECT_MISMATCH / _EVIDENCE_* under FOUNDATION_ACTIVATION_BINDING). Nothing is restamped, so a stale lease stays distinguishable from an absent attempt.
4. agreeingAttempt: store.readEvents(payload.attemptAggregateId) -> readFoundationActivationHistory, then THREE equalities against the binding — record.activationDigest === binding.activationDigest, record.effectIntent.intentId === payload.effectId, record.lease.ownerSessionRef === binding.sessionId. Any mismatch (or an unreadable/absent history) -> JOURNAL_BINDING_MISMATCH. attemptRef/leaseRef come off that agreed record. The caller's aggregate id only LOCATES; these equalities are what forbid pointing at another live attempt.
5. durableNodeKey: readEvents(deriveDispatchAggregateId(attemptAggregateId)), filter to FoundationDispatchReserved, require EXACTLY one, decode -> re-encode -> sameBytes, then textOf(...,"nodeKey"). Zero, two, drifted or missing -> JOURNAL_NODE_UNREADABLE. RESERVED (not RECORDED) because RECORDED is written only at settlement and would be absent mid-attempt.
6. decodeJournalEntries — the step-3 strict decoder — before @moe/context ever sees an entry.
7. readCurrentAttemptJournal(store, binding.activationDigest, projectId). ABSENT is the empty list HERE AND ONLY HERE (the first append); every other refusal propagates with its own code and layer, so an unreadable history is never folded onto as if it were empty.
8. createDeadEndJournal([...prior, ...admitted]). A REFUSED result is carried verbatim — `journalRefusal(journal.code, journal.layer)` = JOURNAL_LIMIT_REACHED / DEAD_END_JOURNAL, with no truncation and no retry with fewer entries.
9. Body from DURABLE facts only: activationDigest (binding), attemptRef + leaseRef (agreed record), effectId, entries + journalDigest (the ADMITTED journal's own canonically ordered entries and its own digest), nodeKey (RESERVED event), projectId + sessionId (envelope/binding), recordVersion, truthClass "DAEMON_VERIFIED". Canonical bytes via encodeFoundationPayload; drift -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED. There is NO path by which a caller-named project, lease, graph, digest, truth class or replacement journal reaches these bytes.
10. commitAppend: ONE event on deriveAttemptJournalAggregateId(binding.activationDigest) at expectedVersion = the CURRENT event count, key {commandId, principalId, projectId}, requestBytes = the caller's original bytes so replay identity is the request itself. Never rewrites a prior event. Non-EFFECTS_COMMITTED or any throw -> JOURNAL_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE, EXCEPT IdempotencyConflictError, which is deliberately RETHROWN so the seam's decision port reports it under its own code and the DURABLE_STORE layer.
11. The accepted answer carries the store's own decision and disposition; every durable value a consumer reads comes back through readCurrentAttemptJournal, never from the value just written.

Verified against packages/store/src/decision-ledger-transaction.ts:86-95,124-132: the decision-key lookup runs BEFORE any expected-version check, so a byte-identical replay returns REPLAYED even though the tail has moved, and the same key with different bytes raises IdempotencyConflictError. That is what makes step 8's replay/conflict pair reachable.

implementationPlan.description:
Land the STRICT CURRENT READER `readCurrentAttemptJournal(store, activationDigest, expectedProjectId)` in the same module. If journal-append.ts would cross 250 physical lines, split the reader into apps/daemon/src/journal/journal-reader.ts plus its .js bridge — that split is AUTHORIZED by this plan; record the measured line count as the forcing evidence in the completion notes, since the per-FILE cap is hard and the per-task file count is not a reason to breach it.
Algorithm, fail-closed at every branch:
- `store.readEvents(deriveAttemptJournalAggregateId(activationDigest))` in try/catch -> JOURNAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE on throw; zero events -> JOURNAL_RECORD_ABSENT (distinct from UNREADABLE: no rows and an unreadable store demand opposite repairs).
- Every event must be `AttemptJournalAppended` with `aggregateSequence === index + 1`; a foreign type or a sequence hole -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED; two events claiming the same sequence -> JOURNAL_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS.
- The CURRENT journal is the LAST event. Decode -> re-encode -> `sameBytes(again.bytes, event.payload)`; drift -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED. Canonical bytes need both the digest and the re-encode.
- Body exact-keyed; recordVersion mismatch -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED; body projectId !== expectedProjectId -> JOURNAL_PROJECT_MISMATCH.
- RE-DERIVE the digest through the production surface: run `createDeadEndJournal(body.entries)` and compare `journal.digest` with the stored `journalDigest`; unequal -> JOURNAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH; REFUSED -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED. This is what makes a stored digest that has quietly stopped covering its entries unusable rather than merely wrong, and it is where the DoD's digest mutation drill lands.
- Answer frozen: `{ ok: true, authority: "DURABLE_JOURNAL", journalDigest, entries, attemptRef, leaseRef, nodeKey, sessionId, effectId, activationDigest }`. Every refused branch returns authority "NONE" and no digest — an unverifiable journal never becomes a handoff input.
Tests: ABSENT before any append; UNREADABLE on a throwing store; MALFORMED on a planted drifted payload; AMBIGUOUS on a duplicated sequence; PROJECT_MISMATCH on a foreign expected project; DIGEST_MISMATCH on a planted body whose entries and digest disagree — each pinning the exact code AND the exact layer.

A REAL PRODUCTION DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED BY THIS STEP — the replay case went red as 409 PORT_REFUSED. `identifyExpectedVersionRequest` (packages/store/src/store-digests.ts:82-95) hashes `expectedVersion` ALONGSIDE the request bytes. My writer derived expectedVersion from the aggregate tail, so the first append moved the tail and a BYTE-IDENTICAL retry supplied expectedVersion 1 where the original supplied 0 — different hash, so `reconcileHistoricalDecision` raised IdempotencyConflictError. A plain retry of an accepted command was indistinguishable from hostile command-id reuse, and the DoD requires the opposite. FIX: read `store.getCommandDecision({commandId, principalId, projectId})` first and reuse `prior.expectedVersion` when a decision already exists, falling back to the tail otherwise. This keeps the STORE the sole authority on identity — same key + same bytes REPLAYS, same key + DIFFERENT bytes still conflicts — and deliberately does NOT copy work-claim's `replayOf`, which returns the stored decision without comparing request bytes and would turn a conflicting retry into a silent success. Recorded as Serena memory `gotcha-expectedversion-is-hashed-into-the-replay-identity`.

REPLAY: same bytes twice -> second is REPLAYED, raw event count read OUT OF THE STORE is still 1, and the reader's entries and journalDigest are identical to the first answer.
CONFLICT: same commandId with DIFFERENT entries -> refused with the store's OWN code IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT under layer DURABLE_STORE, asserted `.not.toBe(DAEMON_JOURNAL_APPEND)`; refused BEFORE mutating (raw count still 1) and the reader still returns the ORIGINAL entries, digest and id list.

The case is non-vacuous by construction: idem-2 occurred FIRST but was appended SECOND, so insertion order and canonical order disagree and the assertion pins ["idem-2","idem-1"].
BOUND CONTROL: a journal AT MAX_JOURNAL_ENTRY_COUNT is ACCEPTED and reads back with 8 entries; one more refuses JOURNAL_LIMIT_REACHED / DEAD_END_JOURNAL with the raw count unchanged. Without the accepted control, "one over refuses" could equally be the daemon rejecting large lists for an unrelated reason.

THE GENERATED HOSTILE SWEEP, split in two because JSON cannot carry everything:
- WIRE SWEEP, 51 cases, generated per entry field (missing / numeric / null / array for each of the 11 keys) plus 7 specials (own `__proto__` key, uppercase digest, occurredAt without Z, NaN text, empty id, nested list, array-like object). Cardinality is asserted BEFORE outcomes — `> 0`, the exact formula `keys*4 + 7`, and all labels distinct — so a sweep that generated nothing cannot pass vacuously. Every case must refuse with a code from the frozen JOURNAL_CODES list under DAEMON_JOURNAL_APPEND, a throw is converted into a NAMED failure ("... CRASHED instead of refusing"), an acceptance into "... was ACCEPTED", and the whole sweep runs on ONE harness so the closing `rows === 0` proves not one of the 51 left durable residue.
  The `__proto__` case was initially VACUOUS and was fixed: `{ ...base, __proto__: x }` in an object literal SETS THE PROTOTYPE and creates no own key, so it serialised as a clean 11-key entry and was ACCEPTED. - REFLECTION SWEEP, 8 cases, driven against the PRODUCTION decoder `decodeJournalEntries` directly, because JSON.stringify invokes a getter, serialises -0 as 0 and throws on a revoked proxy — asserting these at the seam would test the encoder, not the fence. Accessor-bearing entry, non-enumerable own property, revoked-proxy entry, revoked-proxy LIST, -0 predicate version, symbol-keyed entry, class-instance (inherited-prototype) entry, sparse entry list: each refuses JOURNAL_ENTRY_MALFORMED and none throws. 1) ADD A NEW WIRE KIND for the journal. REJECTED by task rail 1 and unnecessary: `journal.append` is already a member of the frozen `RuntimeCommandKind` union at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:96 and is already generated into the control-room client (packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts:218). Annotating the constant as `RuntimeCommandKind` makes a typo a compile error.
2) STORE ONLY THE DELTA ENTRIES per append and fold them on read. REJECTED: the reader would have to reconstruct ordering itself, and the DoD asks for a current reader that answers the attempt-bound digest FROM CANONICAL BYTES. Chosen instead: each append persists the whole admitted journal (canonically ordered entries + its digest) as the new head event, and the READER re-derives the digest through `createDeadEndJournal` and refuses on mismatch. That keeps the durable bytes authoritative while making a digest that has quietly stopped covering its entries unusable rather than merely wrong — and it is where the DoD's required digest mutation drill lands.
3) KEY THE JOURNAL AGGREGATE ON A CALLER-SUPPLIED ATTEMPT AGGREGATE ID. REJECTED: a caller could then name a journal stream into existence. Chosen: derive it from `binding.activationDigest`, which `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding` produces from committed evidence and cross-checks for coherence. The caller's `attemptAggregateId` only LOCATES the activation record; the activation-digest equality check is what forbids pointing at another attempt.
4) LET `createDeadEndJournal` VALIDATE THE ENTRIES. REJECTED, and this is the sharpest hazard in the task: it performs NO shape validation. `clonePredicate` switches on `predicate.kind` and returns `undefined` for an unknown kind, and `canonicalSha256` THROWS `Unsupported canonical value type: undefined`. An unvalidated entry crashes the command instead of refusing it, and a crash is not a refusal. The daemon must decode entries strictly first, importing DEAD_END_KINDS and FactPredicate from @moe/context rather than retyping them.

1) `createDeadEndJournal` CRASHES ON A MALFORMED ENTRY rather than refusing — `clonePredicate` returns undefined for an unknown predicate kind and `canonicalSha256` throws on undefined. If the daemon's strict entry decode is missing or incomplete, the command dies with a TypeError and any test asserting only "did not succeed" stays green. Assert the REFUSAL code, and drill it by deleting the decoder.

2) `cloneEntry` SPREADS the caller's entry, so an extra key would survive into the journal AND into the digest. The exact-key entry decoder is the only thing preventing that; it is not defence in depth, it is the fence.

3) ADDING A WORKSPACE DEPENDENCY. `pnpm install` on this repo has known Windows hazards (a WSL-stamped node_modules kills Windows pnpm). Check `git diff --stat pnpm-lock.yaml` is confined to the apps/daemon importer block; a wide churn means the install did something else and must be reported, not committed.

6) ABSENT IS NOT FATAL IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE — the first append on an attempt with no prior journal. Everywhere else ABSENT is a refusal. A reader that treats ABSENT as empty for its OTHER callers would hand the release path an empty-journal digest for an attempt whose journal is merely unreadable; keep the emptiness decision in the WRITER, not in the reader.

7) THE LEASE DEADLINE IS WALL SECONDS while coordination time is epoch milliseconds, and the scheduler's overdue rule is `seconds > deadline`, so the deadline second itself is still live. An off-by-one here turns a live lease into an expired one; drive the expiry test well past the boundary and assert the code, not just the refusal.
